rationale: Round 2 on 6cdbc374, implementing the guardian's named alternative from the round-1 veto. The defect is unchanged: diagnose_load_runtime reads diagnose_route's forwarded requests and drop counts under the 'route.' namespace by string; a per-workflow override of the route step's output_field silently decouples the two ends and every forwarded request or upstream drop reads as ZERO. Round 1 delivered the check by threading the whole plan through ActionParams and editing buildActionParams; the guardian vetoed THAT DELIVERY (shared, load-bearing infrastructure widened for one pipeline's two-step contract) while explicitly blessing the validation logic and tests. This round re-homes the plan access exactly as the veto's notes prescribe: the ActionParams field and the coordinator line are REMOVED (walked back in commit 3af7b9d8d, on top of the already-live 6f7e69d22), and diagnose_load_runtime reads ITS OWN orchestration's workflow_plan->steps from the DB — a diagnosis-pipeline-local read using the DB handle and orchestration id the action already holds. validateRouteWiring and its falsification tests are unchanged. The round-1 objections from editquality, reuse_agent and prior_art are each answered in this submission: skip paths are now LOGGED (never silent); the searches the seats asked for were run and are quoted in grounded_in (no existing workflow-plan validator exists; no existing plan-level field on ActionParams existed before round 1 added one); and the diagnose_state/iteration coupling question is answered — that is the ROUTE step's own read-back of its prior state (state_field config on diagnose_route, which its own config comment says must track the route step's output_field), a self-coupling inside one step, not part of this reader's cross-step contract; extending a guard there would live inside diagnose_route and is out of scope here.

plan.summary: Walk back the round-1 shared-infrastructure delivery (remove ActionParams.WorkflowSteps and the buildActionParams line) and re-home the route-wiring check inside the diagnosis pipeline's own boundary: diagnose_load_runtime loads its own orchestration's workflow_plan->'steps' with one indexed SELECT per gather and feeds the UNCHANGED validateRouteWiring. Every skip path (no orchestration id, row missing, parse failure) logs a warning naming the guard as skipped. The check deliberately runs on EVERY gather, not only the first: plans are immutable per orchestration in practice so later iterations are redundant, but the re-check is one indexed SELECT and keeps the action stateless; this is a stated choice, not an accident.

edits.rationale: The guardian's objection #1: ActionParams is the shared contract for every action in every pipeline; the round-1 field handed every action read visibility into the whole plan, constrained only by a comment. Removed entirely.

The guardian's objection #2: buildActionParams is the core dispatch path for every step of every workflow; it should not carry a diagnose-specific concern. The round-1 line is removed; the function returns to its pre-6f7e69d22 shape.

edits.rationale: The re-homed plan access: the action reads its OWN orchestration's persisted plan. Pipeline-local by construction — no other action, no shared struct, no coordinator involvement. The action already holds params.DB and its orchestration id.

The call site: guard before any route.* read; and per editquality's round-1 objection, the skip path is LOGGED, never silent — a guard that vanishes quietly is the failure shape it exists to catch. A wiring divergence still fails the gather loudly.

plan.risks: 1) One indexed SELECT per gather iteration added to the diagnosis loop (bounded: gathers per run are capped by max_iterations; the action already runs several queries per gather). 2) The guard's availability now depends on the orchestration row being readable from inside the action — if a future refactor moves plan storage, the guard degrades to a LOGGED skip, not a silent one, which is the designed failure mode. 3) The route step's own diagnose_state read-back remains unguarded (answered above as out of this reader's contract — a route-internal self-coupling; a future guard there belongs inside diagnose_route). 4) The walked-back commit necessarily touched coordinator.go and types/context.go, which carried a concurrent session's in-flight bugs_open/060 work — included and attributed in the commit message to keep HEAD compiling (their coordinator hunk references the context.go field); reviewers should note that passenger is 060's thread's work, not part of this plan.
